speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) what has been the trend of scam crimes in the past 10 years; and (b) what is the Police's strategy to reduce such scam crimes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Police started to track the number and types of scams from 2016 when it started to become a crime of concern.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Member asked about what the Singapore Police Force is doing about this.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: MHA adopts a multi-pronged approach to tackle scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Police have set up specialised units to disrupt scammers’ operations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: One of these units is the E-Commerce Fraud Enforcement and Coordination Team or E-FECT in short.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Since its formation in November 2018, the E-FECT has arrested 101 e-commerce scammers and solved about 2,000 e-commerce scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: In June 2019, the Police set up the Anti-Scam Centre or ASC, which acts as a nerve centre for investigations into scam-related crimes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The ASC’s focus is to mitigate victims’ losses, through the swift interdiction of the proceeds of the crime.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Second, the Police have stepped up collaboration with foreign law enforcement agencies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Police set up the Transnational Commercial Crime Task Force or TCTF in short, in October 2017 to investigate transnational scams such as China Officials Impersonation Scams, Internet Love Scams and Credit-for-Sex Scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: To date, the TCTF has conducted 12 joint operations with international counterparts, resulting in the arrests of over 120 suspects.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: First, in November 2019, the TCTF worked with the Royal Malaysia Police, Hong Kong Police Force and the Macau Judiciary Police to jointly cripple an Internet Love Scam syndicate based in Malaysia.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The group is believed to have been involved in at least 139 cases in Singapore, Malaysia, Hong Kong and Macau, involving losses of about S$5.8 million.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Second, in May 2019, the TCTF successfully extradited two Nigerian men to Singapore for cheating Singapore-based victims in Internet Love Scams perpetrated from Malaysia.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The two accused persons were charged in court in May 2019, and the trial is still on-going.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Third, we work closely with public and private sector stakeholders.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Police regularly engage banks, remittance agencies and convenience stores to train their frontline staff to spot possible scam victims.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: In 2019, the Police commended 108 recipients from the community for preventing 91 instances of scams involving approximately S$5 million.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Earlier this year, the Inter-Ministry Committee on Scams was set up to coordinate a whole-of-Government effort to combat scams and their roles include (a) to improve scam detection and disruption capabilities; (b) to develop measures to secure the digital space; (c) to enhance the loss recovery and remediation experience for scam victims; and (iv) to improve public education and outreach efforts against scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Police and the National Crime Prevention Council have disseminated advisories through various media platforms, including messaging and social media platforms such as Facebook, Instagram and TikTok.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: In August 2020, an anti-scam public education campaign, "Spot the Signs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: This new campaign focuses on sharing real-life scam examples to educate and inform the public on how to spot the tell-tale signs of various scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Indeed, the key to fight against scams is a discerning public.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: They are urged to stay vigilant and report possible scams promptly to the Police.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: First, I heard a few types of scams mentioned by the Minister of State.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: Can the Minister of State advise us which is the most common scam and which is the one that has the biggest monetary loss in Singapore?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: I understand that five major crimes which are often communicated to the communities have dropped significantly over the years, and the number of online scams has overtaken the five crimes.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: So, will the Minister of State consider providing the number or type of online crimes by constituency, on a monthly basis, so as to better alert the residents and garner their support to fight and prevent online scams.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: Thirdly, I often receive WhatsApp messages asking me to take personal loans from moneylenders.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: I think it is mostly the works of the illegal moneylenders.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: I also receive phone calls to tell me that I have a parcel stuck at the custom and mostly this is a fraud case.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: I understand many Singaporeans also receive similar messages.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: Can the Police advise Singaporeans what to do when they receive such messages or phone calls?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: Can the Police consider setting up a hotline or an email account for Singaporeans to send such messages and details of the phone calls to the Police?

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: With the prevalence of Internet and the e-commerce platform, this has become the number one, the most common scam that we see in our community.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: The second one is social media, impersonation scam.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: These are in terms of the number of incidents that happened.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: If you would like to see more in terms of the top 10, you can go to our anti-scam website.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: We have listed the most common scams that have happened.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: The Member also asked in terms of breaking down online scams by constituency.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: So, I am not so sure how this breakdown will help but we will certainly take a look at the Member's suggestions on how to break down the data.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: If it is useful, we will do that as well.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: Working with National Crime Prevention Council, since several years ago, we have already set up a hotline.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: Any member of the public who needs help, who is not sure, who needs advice on whether that is a scam, they can go to the hotline.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: On top of that, we have also set up the scamalert.sg, which is a URL that allows members of the public to see what are the most common scams that have happened and also for members of the public to share their stories about how they have fallen prey to scams.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: So, these are the efforts that we will continue to step up, in time to come.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: I just want to make two small clarifications about what I said.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: So, I am suggesting that the Police can do the same for the number of online scams by constituency and let the residents know that these are the online crimes that happened in their neighbourhood, where their neighbour are victims, so that they are more aware, and they can help the Police to fight the online crime together.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: The second one, I mentioned that we often receive a lot of messages.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: Is there some way or can we set up a website, and we can send those phone calls and messages to that one site, rather than just making phone call which is sometimes, not efficient because you need people to man the hotline.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: As I had mentioned, we will take his suggestions.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: Today, the Police work closely with the community to also highlight what are the top five crimes in the community.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: Scam is obviously one of those that are increasing in trend.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: So, we will take the Member's suggestions in mind.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: The second one with regard to the website and a one-stop station for residents to post and also to submit the scam situation, as I had mentioned, the scamalert.sg would probably serve that purpose.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: Indeed, the Member has highlighted a vulnerable group.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: We are also mindful that they are quite prone to scams.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: So, these are the efforts that we are working on and we will continue to make sure that our seniors are protected in cyberspace.
